decisive_items: 20×20 mm round cystic mass at the base of the tongue
33×31×27 mm well-defined cystic lesion in the midline of the tongue base
complete pharyngeal airway obstruction during both inspiration and expiration as the mass pulled the epiglottis down and backward
response.rationale: The tongue-base cystic mass is the primary structural lesion causing airway compromise and secondary obstructive sleep apnea; hypertension and diabetes are unrelated comorbidities, and OSA is a downstream syndrome rather than the underlying diagnosis.

rejected.why: Mild hypertension is a comorbidity, not the presenting diagnosis.
Diabetes is a comorbidity, not the presenting diagnosis.
Obstructive sleep apnea is present but is caused by the tongue-base cyst, so it is not the most likely primary diagnosis.
